content: It includes citations from various studies, articles, and reports related to HIV care, antiretroviral therapy, family planning, and other public health topics. 1. A study conducted in Jinja, southeast Uganda, compared virological failure rates in patients treated under a home-based HIV care model versus a facility-based model. This cluster-randomized equivalence trial was published in The Lancet in 2009. 2. Strategies to improve patient retention on antiretroviral therapy in sub-Saharan Africa were explored in a 2010 article in Tropical Medicine & International Health. The authors emphasized the importance of tailored interventions to address barriers to care. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released global recommendations and guidelines on task-shifting, which involve delegating specific healthcare tasks to non-specialist health workers. These guidelines were accessed in November 2015. 4. A 2015 study by Vojnov and the Clinton Health Access Initiative evaluated whether specimen collection and diagnostic testing performed by non-laboratory professionals, including lay providers, yielded comparable patient and program outcomes to those conducted by laboratory professionals. 5. WHO recommendations for clinical mentoring to support the scale-up of HIV care, antiretroviral therapy, and prevention in resource-constrained settings were published and accessed in November 2015. 6. A Cochrane review in 2013 examined the decentralization of HIV treatment in lowand middle-income countries, highlighting the potential benefits of bringing care closer to patients. 7. Barriers to accessing highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) among HIV-positive women attending antenatal clinics in western Uganda were investigated in a 2010 study published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 8. Factors influencing access to HIV care and treatment within prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) programs in urban Zimbabwe were analyzed in a 2010 study, also published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 9. A stepped-wedge evaluation published in AIDS in 2010 demonstrated that integrating antiretroviral therapy into antenatal care increased treatment initiation among HIV-infected pregnant women. 10. A 2012 study compared maternal and child health clinic models with HIV comprehensive care clinic models for providing services to HIV-exposed infants. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 11. The integration of HIV and antenatal care services during pregnancy in Kenya was studied in a cluster-randomized controlled trial. The design, methods, and baseline results were published in PLoS One in 2012. 12. Patient satisfaction with integrated HIV and antenatal care services in rural Kenya was assessed in a 2012 study published in AIDS Care. 13. A 2010 study in BMC Public Health compared two service delivery models for PMTCT during the transition from single-dose nevirapine to multi-drug antiretroviral regimens. 14. The acceptability and feasibility of integrating HIV care services into antenatal clinics in rural Kenya were explored through qualitative provider interviews, with findings published in Global Public Health in 2012. 15. The WHO's 2015 global tuberculosis report and its recommendations on integrating HIV and TB services were accessed to inform public health strategies. 16. A cohort study in Indonesia examined the integration of methadone maintenance treatment and HIV care for injecting drug users, with results published in Acta Medica Indonesiana in 2009. 17. A randomized trial compared clinic-based treatment of opioid-dependent HIV-infected patients with referral to an opioid treatment program. The findings were published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2010. 18. Depression among pregnant rural South African women undergoing HIV testing was studied, with results published in JAMA in 2006. 19. A 2008 study in AIDS Care investigated repeated pregnancies among women with known HIV status in Pune, India. 20. High pregnancy intentions and missed opportunities for patient-provider communication about fertility were identified in a South African cohort of HIV-positive women on antiretroviral therapy, as reported in AIDS Behavior in 2012. 21. A cross-sectional survey in Uganda examined the uptake of family planning methods and unplanned pregnancies among HIV-infected individuals, with findings published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2011. 22. A 2013 study in AIDS Research and Treatment explored the perspectives of HIV-positive men in Kenya on overcoming barriers to family planning through service integration. 23. The integration of family planning services into HIV care and treatment programs in Kenya was evaluated in a cluster-randomized trial, with results published in AIDS in 2013. 24. The cost-effectiveness of integrating family planning and HIV services was analyzed in a 2013 study published in AIDS. 25. A systematic review in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2012 assessed the costs and efficiency of integrating HIV/AIDS services with other health services. 26. A 2014 study in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses found that the age at antiretroviral therapy initiation predicted immune recovery, mortality, and loss to follow-up among HIV-infected adults in urban Zambia. 27. A 2012 study in PLoS One examined antiretroviral therapy outcomes among adolescents and youth in rural Zimbabwe. 28. The treatment and care needs of adolescents living with HIV were discussed at the 18th International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa in 2015. 29. A 2014 study in AIDS Behavior evaluated the use of cell phone support for non-adherent HIV-infected youth and young adults. 30. The long-term effects of a preconception counseling program on family planning intentions and behaviors in teens with diabetes were reported in Diabetes Care in 2013. 31. A 2011 exploratory study in Public Health evaluated the provision of additional midwifery support to teenage mothers. 32. A 2009 community-based randomized trial in Annals of Family Medicine tested a motivational intervention to reduce rapid subsequent births among adolescent mothers.
